units.title: Familiar faces
units.subtitle: А М О Т К Н

pages.title: First word
pages.intro: Three letters that look and sound the way you expect. By the end of this page you will write a Russian word.

exercises.text: Read straight through, sound by sound: м + а = ма.

pages.title: Т and К
pages.intro: Two more familiar shapes, and you can read real words: there, cat, how, who.

pages.title: Н: looks like H
pages.intro: Н looks like H but says n. With it come he, she and it.

exercises.text: Н looks like H and sounds like n, so он reads on. In она́ and оно́ the stress is on the end, and the first о relaxes toward a: ana, ano.

units.title: I, you, we
units.subtitle: я ты мы вы они́

pages.title: Я and Ы
pages.intro: Я is a whole word: I. Ы is a brand-new sound, and it gives you you and we.

exercises.text: Ы has no English twin: say ee, then pull your tongue back without moving your lips. You hear it in ты and мы.

pages.title: И and В
pages.intro: И looks like a backwards N and says ee. В looks like B and says v. Together: you, they, and.

options: Here are the cat and mom.

pages.title: All the pronouns
pages.intro: Eight little words: I, you, he, she, it, we, you, they. Write each from memory.

exercises.text: Ты is one person you know well; вы is several people, or one person you address politely.
Я, ты, он, она́, оно́, мы, вы, они́.

units.title: This is…
units.subtitle: э́то, не, нет · Р С

pages.title: Э and Е
pages.intro: Э says e as in bet and starts the most useful word in Russian, э́то. Е says ye and gives you no.

exercises.text: Э is a plain e. Е is ye at the start of a word, and after a consonant it is e that softens the consonant, as in не and нет. Э́то means this is or that is, with no verb needed.

exercises.prompt: What is this, and what is it not? Point at two things: Э́то… Э́то не…

pages.title: Р: looks like P
pages.intro: Р is a tapped r: the tip of the tongue flicks once behind the teeth. Now: world, cake, rocket.

exercises.prompt: Name three things in the room with э́то.

pages.title: С, and the lazy о
pages.intro: С looks like C and always says s. Unstressed о has a surprise too.

exercises.text: Only a stressed о is a full o. Unstressed, it relaxes to a: окно́ sounds like akno, она́ like ana.

options: This is not cheese, this is cake.

exercises.prompt: Who is this? Introduce two people or animals.

units.title: Where?
units.subtitle: У Д Г Л · тут, там, где

pages.title: У and Д
pages.intro: У looks like y and says oo. Д is a little house that says d: yes, house, water.

exercises.prompt: Who is at home right now, and who is not?

pages.title: Г and где?
pages.intro: Г is an upside-down L and says g as in go. Its best word is где, where.

exercises.text: In the present, Russian leaves out is, and it asks questions without do: Где кот? is Where is the cat?

exercises.prompt: Ask where two things are, and answer.

pages.title: Л: a tent
pages.intro: Л says l and brings the table and the milk.

options: Where is the table? It is here.
Where is the milk? It is there.

exercises.prompt: What is here and what is there? Three short sentences.

pages.title: Who? Where? How?
pages.intro: No new letters: questions and answers with everything so far.

exercises.text: Кто там? Э́то ма́ма. Ма́ма до́ма. А где кот? Кот тут.
exercises.en: Who is there? It's mom. Mom is at home. And where is the cat? The cat is here.

options: And where is the cat? The cat is here.
And who is the cat? The cat is mom.
And where is mom? Mom is at home.

exercises.prompt: A tiny dialogue: who is there, where is the cat?

units.title: New shapes
units.subtitle: П Б Й Ё Ю

pages.title: П and Б
pages.intro: П is a doorway and says p. Б looks like a 6 and says b. They bring dad, soup and thank you.

options: This is a brother. This is not a robot.
This is a robot. This is not a brother.

exercises.prompt: Who is in your family? Name them.

pages.title: Й and Ё: mine
pages.intro: Й is the short y at the end of boy: мой, my. Ё says yo and is always stressed.

exercises.text: My follows the thing it owns: мой for a consonant ending, моя́ for -а, моё for -о.

exercises.prompt: Three things that are yours, with мой, моя́ or моё.

pages.title: Ю and the vowel pairs
pages.intro: Ю says yu, and completes a pattern: each plain vowel has a y-partner.

exercises.text: Five vowels come in pairs, hard and soft: а/я, у/ю, э/е, о/ё, ы/и. At the start of a word or after a vowel (моя́, моё), я, ю, е and ё begin with a y. After a consonant the soft letters make the consonant itself soft (three you will meet later always stay hard).

exercises.prompt: What do you love? Two or three things.

units.title: Hushing sounds
units.subtitle: Ч Ш Ж Щ Х

pages.title: Ч: what?
pages.intro: Ч says ch as in chair. In что, what, it is said sh: shto.

exercises.text: Что is spelled with ч but said shto. Что э́то? is the question you will ask most.

exercises.prompt: What is this? Ask and answer about two things, and say what you are reading.

pages.title: Ш and Ж
pages.intro: Ш is three teeth: sh. Ж is a beetle: zh, as in pleasure.

exercises.text: То́же means too or also, and наш means our.

exercises.prompt: What is on the table at home? Use наш and то́же.

pages.title: Щ and Х
pages.intro: Щ is a long soft sh and gives you ещё, more. Х is the ch of Scottish loch and gives you хорошо́, good.

exercises.text: Х is a breathy kh from the back of the throat. Хорошо́ has three о but only the last is full: kha-ra-SHO.

exercises.prompt: How are things? Answer, and say what there is more of.

units.title: The last letters
units.subtitle: З Ь Ц Ф Ъ

pages.title: З and Ь
pages.intro: З looks like a 3 and says z. Ь has no sound of its own: it softens the consonant before it.

exercises.text: Ь softens the consonant before it, as if a tiny y were starting. Compare брат with мать: the т of мать is soft.

exercises.prompt: Who is in your family, and what do you know?

pages.title: Ц and Ф
pages.intro: Ц is ts as in cats. Ф is a circle on a pole: f. Now: fact, coffee, street.

options: Where is father? He is at home.
Where is the street? It is there.
Who is father? He is here.

exercises.prompt: Coffee, a street, a fact: three sentences with the new words.

pages.title: Hello, and the hard sign
pages.intro: Приве́т and пока́: hi and bye at home. And the last letter, Ъ, a silent wall.

exercises.text: Приве́т is hi and пока́ is bye, for anyone you call ты. До за́втра is see you tomorrow.
Ъ makes no sound: it keeps a consonant apart from the я, е, ё or ю after it, so объе́кт is ab-YEKT. It is rare, and it makes 33.

exercises.prompt: Say hi to someone, ask how they are, say bye.

pages.title: The whole alphabet
pages.intro: All 33 letters at once: words from every corner of the alphabet.

exercises.text: Лук and люк have the same oo sound; the difference you hear is the л, hard in лук and soft in люк. The vowel letter is only how the spelling shows it.

exercises.prompt: Your favourite word so far, and why you like it (in Russian as far as you can).

pages.title: By ear: hard and soft
pages.intro: Pairs of words that differ by one soft consonant, and the voiced letters that go quiet at the end of a word.

exercises.text: A soft consonant is not a consonant plus y: the middle of the tongue rises toward the roof of the mouth while you say it. Брат and брать differ only in that т. At the end of a word, and before a voiceless consonant, б, в, г, д, ж, з lose their voice: хлеб ends in a p, ло́жка says losh-ka.
Брат, брать. Лук, люк. Был, бил.

exercises.prompt: Write about bread, cheese and tea on a table.

units.title: At the table
units.subtitle: до́брое у́тро · прия́тного аппети́та · пожа́луйста

pages.title: Good morning
pages.intro: The phrases that open and close the day.

exercises.text: До́брое у́тро in the morning, до́брый ве́чер in the evening, споко́йной но́чи at bedtime.

exercises.prompt: Good morning: what you say when you wake up, and what you say at night.

pages.title: Enjoy your meal
pages.intro: Прия́тного аппети́та is what you say as the food arrives. Then: is it good?

exercises.text: Прия́тного аппети́та is enjoy your meal; the reply is спаси́бо, и тебе́. Вку́сно means it's tasty.

exercises.prompt: Dinner is on the table. What do you say, and is it good?

pages.title: Please, and more
pages.intro: Пожа́луйста is please and also you're welcome. Ещё asks for more.

exercises.text: Пожа́луйста is said pa-ZHA-lu-sta, often just pa-ZHAL-sta. It is also the answer to спаси́бо.

exercises.prompt: Ask for more of something, politely, and say thank you.

units.title: Keeping up
units.subtitle: я не понима́ю · ещё раз · как по-ру́сски?

pages.title: When you don't understand
pages.intro: Phrases that keep a conversation going when you are lost. Learn them whole; the grammar inside comes later.

exercises.text: Я не понима́ю is I don't understand. Ещё раз, пожа́луйста asks for it once more, and поме́дленнее, пожа́луйста asks for it slower.
Как э́то по-ру́сски? asks for a word; что зна́чит…? asks what one means.

examples.en: How do you say this in Russian?

exercises.hint: How do you say this in Russian?

exercises.text: Я не понима́ю. Ещё раз, пожа́луйста.

exercises.prompt: You didn't understand. Write what you would say.

units.title: Breakfast and dinner
units.subtitle: за́втрак, у́жин, хочу́

pages.title: Breakfast and dinner
pages.intro: Two meals, two words, and the question what's for dinner?

exercises.text: За́втрак is breakfast, у́жин is dinner. Что на у́жин? asks what's for dinner.
У́жин гото́в! На у́жин суп и хлеб.

exercises.prompt: What is for breakfast today? And for dinner?

pages.title: I want: хочу́
pages.intro: Хоте́ть, to want, is irregular, but two forms do most of the work: хочу́ and хо́чешь.

exercises.text: Я хочу́ is I want; хо́чешь? is do you want? What you want comes after: хочу́ ко́фе.

options: No, I don't want any, thanks.

exercises.prompt: What do you want right now? Two sentences with хочу́.

pages.title: Table talk
pages.intro: A whole little meal in Russian, from good morning to thank you.

exercises.text:
— До́брое у́тро! Ко́фе?
— Да, пожа́луйста.
— Вот ко́фе, хлеб и сыр.
— Спаси́бо! О́чень вку́сно.
— Ещё ко́фе?
— Нет, спаси́бо.
exercises.en: “Good morning! Coffee?” “Yes, please.” “Here's coffee, bread and cheese.” “Thank you! Very tasty.” “More coffee?” “No, thanks.”

exercises.prompt: A whole little meal: from good morning to thank you.

pages.title: Coffee with milk
pages.intro: С is with; мне is for me. Two small words for every breakfast.

exercises.text: С means with, and the word after it changes: молоко́, с молоко́м; са́хар, с са́харом. Мне is for me: мне чай, пожа́луйста.

options: Tea for me, and coffee for you?
Coffee for me, and tea for you?
Do you want coffee or tea?

exercises.prompt: Order coffee or tea the way you like it.

pages.title: What would you say?
pages.intro: Moments at the table. Each has one phrase from these pages that fits: write it, then check.

exercises.en: Your housemate offers you coffee. Say yes, please.
You'd like more porridge. Ask whether you may have more.
Someone thanks you. Say you're welcome.

exercises.hint: Enjoy your meal! — Thanks, you too!

exercises.en: You didn't catch that. Ask for it once more, please.

exercises.text: Хо́чешь ко́фе? Нет, спаси́бо, я хочу́ чай.

exercises.prompt: What did you eat today?

pages.title: хоте́ть, есть, дать — and с + чем?
pages.intro: Four verbs keep their own tables, and the word for «with» asks for the instrumental.

exercises.text: хоте́ть runs on conjugation I in the singular and II in the plural: хочу́, хо́чешь, хо́чет, хоти́м, хоти́те, хотя́т. есть (to eat) and дать (to give) are older still: ем, ешь, ест; дам, дашь, даст. Переда́й is the imperative of переда́ть.
With: с + instrumental. Masculine and neuter nouns take -ом: с молоко́м, с са́харом; feminine -ой: с ма́мой.
Переда́й мне са́хар, пожа́луйста. Я хочу́ ко́фе с са́харом.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: It: он, она́, оно́
units.subtitle: gender by ending

pages.title: He, she, it
pages.intro: Every thing is он, она́ or оно́, and the last letter usually tells you which.

exercises.text: Consonant at the end: он; -а or -я: она́; -о or -е: оно́; -ь can be он or она́. Па́па is он: meaning beats ending.

exercises.hint: Where is the table? Here it is.
Where is the book? Here it is.
Where is the window? Here it is.

options: Where is the robot? Here she is.
Where is the robot? Here it is.

exercises.prompt: Three things around you: is each он, она́ or оно́? Say where each is.

pages.title: On the table
pages.intro: Table things and their genders. Each one with мой, моя́ or моё.

exercises.text: Ко́фе ends in -е but is masculine: мой ко́фе. Everything else here follows its ending.
Э́то мой ко́фе, а э́то твой чай.

exercises.prompt: What is on your table? Each thing with мой, моя́ or моё.

pages.title: Э́то + anything
pages.intro: Э́то points at anything, and it never changes.

exercises.hint: This is not a table, it's a chair.

exercises.text: Что э́то? Э́то стол. А э́то? Э́то не стол, э́то стул. Где моя́ ча́шка? Вот она́.
exercises.en: What is this? It's a table. And this? It's not a table, it's a chair. Where is my cup? Here it is.

options: This is not a chair, it's a table.
This is not a table, it's a chair.

exercises.prompt: Describe the room: this is…, this is not…

pages.title: Two cups: plurals
pages.intro: More than one: most plurals end in -ы or -и.

exercises.text: A consonant adds -ы and -а becomes -ы: стол, столы́; -я and -ь become -и. After к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ it is always -и, never -ы: ча́шка, ча́шки. Neuter -о becomes -а, and the stress can move: окно́, о́кна.

options: The spoons are here, and the cups are there.
The spoon is here, and the cup is there.
The cups are here, and the spoons are there.

exercises.prompt: Count what you see: cups, spoons, books, windows.

pages.title: A new cup: но́вый, но́вая, но́вое
pages.intro: Describing words follow the noun's gender, just like мой.

exercises.text: Adjectives match the noun: но́вый стол, но́вая ча́шка, но́вое окно́, and for plurals но́вые ча́шки. Ста́рый, old, works the same way.
Мой стол ста́рый, а стул но́вый.

exercises.prompt: Describe three things as new or old.

pages.title: Three declensions
pages.intro: Every noun belongs to one of three tables. The ending of the dictionary form tells you which.

exercises.text: Nouns I end in -а or -я (кни́га, ку́хня), nouns II in a consonant, -й, -ь or in -о, -е (стол, окно́), nouns III in -ь and are feminine (ночь, соль). The table decides every other ending the word will ever take.
Стол, столы́. Окно́, о́кна. Кни́га, кни́ги.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: One to five
pages.intro: Оди́н, два, три, четы́ре, пять. Count something on the table.

exercises.text: Оди́н changes with gender like мой: оди́н стол, одна́ ча́шка.

exercises.prompt: How many of what is on your table? Count to five.

pages.title: Six to ten
pages.intro: Шесть, семь, во́семь, де́вять, де́сять. The soft sign ends every one of them.

exercises.text: Each of these ends in a soft т or м: listen for the little y-colour at the end.

exercises.prompt: Count the things in your room, up to ten.

pages.title: Counting from memory
pages.intro: All ten, out of order. Write the Russian before you say it.

exercises.text: Де́сять, де́вять, во́семь, семь, шесть, пять, четы́ре, три, два, оди́н!

exercises.prompt: Three small sums, written out in words.

pages.title: Eleven to twenty
pages.intro: Eleven to nineteen are a number on ten: оди́ннадцать is one-on-ten.

exercises.text: Eleven to nineteen are the number plus -на́дцать; два becomes две, and a final ь drops: двена́дцать, пятна́дцать. The stress falls on that на except in оди́ннадцать and четы́рнадцать. Twenty is два́дцать.
Оди́ннадцать, двена́дцать, трина́дцать, четы́рнадцать, пятна́дцать, шестна́дцать, семна́дцать, восемна́дцать, девятна́дцать, два́дцать.

exercises.prompt: How old are the people and pets at home? Numbers to twenty.

units.title: Questions
units.subtitle: кто? что? где? как? да и́ли нет?

pages.title: Who and what
pages.intro: Кто is for people and animals, что for things.

exercises.text: Кто? asks about people and animals, even a cat. Что? asks about everything else.

examples.en: Who is this? It's the cat.
What is this? It's a spoon.

exercises.hint: Who is there? It's my brother.

exercises.prompt: Ask three questions with кто and что.

pages.title: Where and how
pages.intro: Где asks where; как asks how. Как дела́? is how are you.

exercises.text: Как дела́? is how are you, between people who know each other. Answer хорошо́ (good) or норма́льно (fine).
Как дела́? Хорошо́, спаси́бо. А у тебя́?

options: Where is the bread? It's there.
Where is the bread? It's here.

exercises.prompt: Ask someone how they are and where something is; answer both.

pages.title: Yes or no
pages.intro: A yes/no question is a statement with a rising voice. Answer да or нет.

exercises.text: Э́то чай. is a statement; Э́то чай? with the voice rising on чай is a question. Nothing else changes.

exercises.hint: Is this soup? No, it's porridge.

exercises.prompt: Two yes/no questions and their answers.

pages.title: When? How many?
pages.intro: Two more question words: когда́, when, and ско́лько, how many or how much.

exercises.text: Когда́? asks when, ско́лько? how many or how much. Ско́лько бу́дет два плюс три? is what is two plus three.
Ско́лько бу́дет пять плюс пять? Де́сять.

exercises.prompt: When is breakfast, and how many cups are there? Ask and answer.

units.title: Mine and yours
units.subtitle: мой, твой, наш, ваш · у меня́ есть

pages.title: My and your
pages.intro: Твой is your for one person you know well, and it changes exactly like мой.

exercises.text: мой / моя́ / моё and твой / твоя́ / твоё: the same split as он / она́ / оно́.

exercises.prompt: Whose things are these? Yours and mine.

pages.title: Our and your
pages.intro: Наш and ваш follow the same pattern: на́ша, на́ше, ва́ша, ва́ше.

exercises.text: Наш is our, ваш is your when you say вы. Both add -а and -е: на́ша, на́ше, ва́ша, ва́ше.

exercises.prompt: Describe your home with наш and на́ша.

pages.title: I have: у меня́ есть
pages.intro: Russian says by me there is: у меня́ есть. It is the everyday I have.

exercises.text: У меня́ есть is literally by me there is. Swap in тебя́ for you: у тебя́ есть.
У меня́ есть брат и сестра́.

exercises.hint: Do you have salt? Yes, I do.

exercises.prompt: What do you have at home? Three sentences with у меня́ есть.

pages.title: I don't have: у меня́ нет
pages.intro: For none, есть becomes нет, and the thing you lack changes its ending.

exercises.text: Swap есть for нет and change the ending: a consonant adds -а (хлеб, хле́ба), -й becomes -я (чай, ча́я), and -о becomes -а. -а becomes -ы, or -и after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ, and -ь becomes -и (соль, со́ли). Ко́фе never changes.

examples.en: There's no tea and no cheese.

exercises.text: У тебя́ есть молоко́? Нет, молока́ нет.

exercises.prompt: What is there none of today? Use у меня́ нет.

pages.title: у меня́ есть: the pronouns change
pages.intro: Having is said as «at me there is». The person stands in the genitive; here is the whole table for я and ты.

exercises.text: Each pronoun has six forms, learned as words. After у (at) and нет (there is no) comes the genitive: меня́, тебя́. The accusative, the object, looks the same: Он зна́ет меня́.
У меня́ есть брат. А у тебя́?

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: Cursive
units.subtitle: про́писи · how Russians write by hand

pages.title: Joined up: о а с е
pages.intro: Russians write by hand in a joined, slanted cursive that looks nothing like print. Start with the round letters: each begins at the top, and the red joins between letters are part of the word.

exercises.text: Cursive о is one oval, round anticlockwise from the top. а is the same oval with a stem down its right side; с and е leave at the bottom right, ready for the next letter.

exercises.prompt: Three round words, written in cursive if you can.

pages.title: The zigzag letters: и ш л м
pages.intro: In a quick hand и, ш, л and м all turn into one zigzag. The school hand keeps them apart: и and ш start at the top with cups, л and м start with a hook on the line.

exercises.text: и: down, cup, up, down, cup; ш is the same with three cups. л and м begin with a little hook on the baseline and climb, and that hook is what tells лиши́шься apart.

exercises.prompt: Write ма́ма and мир in your own hand; add one more word with л or м.

pages.title: Humps and tails: т п н ц щ
pages.intro: т in cursive is three humps, like a Latin m, while ш is three cups. п has one hump, н a tiny loop in the middle; ц and щ end with a tail below the line.

exercises.text: Humps are rounded at the top, cups at the bottom: that is the whole difference between т and ш. н goes down, back up to the middle, a tiny loop, then across. ц and щ finish with a small tail under the line.

exercises.prompt: Where is the table, and what is on it? Two sentences, joined up.

pages.title: Loops below the line: д у з р ф
pages.intro: Several letters drop below the line in cursive. д is an oval with a loop under it, like a g; у and з loop under too; р and ф send a long stem down.

exercises.text: Cursive д has no feet: it is an oval whose stem drops below the line and loops back. у does the same after its cup, з curls into a loop, and р and ф put a long stem under the line.

exercises.prompt: Your morning in two short sentences, in cursive.

pages.title: Above the line: б в к
pages.intro: б climbs above the small letters and flags to the right; в loops above the line and closes its bowl at the top. к stays small, with an arm and a leg.

exercises.text: б: an oval, then its stem rises and flags right. в starts at the middle, loops above the line, comes down and closes its bowl at the top of the small letters. к: down, back up to the middle, a short arm, then the leg.

exercises.prompt: Who is your brother or sister, and what do they love?

pages.title: Capitals and names
pages.intro: Capital letters in cursive are the big school shapes: an А with a hook, a Т with a wavy roof, a Д that loops at its foot. Sentences start with them.

exercises.text: А starts with a hook on the line like л, climbs, comes down, and gets its bar last. Т takes its roof first, then the stem. Э, З, С and О are the rounds you know, taller.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences that start with a capital letter: Э́то… Вот…

pages.title: A note on the table
pages.intro: A note someone left: short, joined, slanted. Read it, copy it in cursive, and write one back.

exercises.text: Notes are written fast: letters lean, joins stretch, the pen barely lifts. Look for the hooks of л and м, the humps of т, the loops under д and у.

exercises.prompt: Leave a note on the table for someone at home.

units.title: Doing things
units.subtitle: чита́ть, ду́мать, знать

pages.title: Reading: я чита́ю
pages.intro: One verb, six endings. Learn them on чита́ть, to read, and they work for hundreds of verbs.

exercises.text: Drop -ть from чита́ть and add the ending for who is doing it: я -ю, ты -ешь, он and она́ -ет. Notice that кни́га becomes кни́гу when it is the thing being read.

options: He is thinking about a book.

exercises.prompt: What are you reading today? Who else is reading?

pages.title: We, you, they
pages.intro: The plural endings: мы чита́ем, вы чита́ете, они́ чита́ют.

exercises.text: мы чита́ем, вы чита́ете, они́ чита́ют. Ду́мать, to think, works the same way.

exercises.prompt: What do we read, and what do they think?

pages.title: Knowing: знать
pages.intro: Знать, to know, has the same endings. Я зна́ю and я не зна́ю carry a lot of conversations.

exercises.text: Не goes right before the verb: я не зна́ю, I don't know.

exercises.hint: Do you know where the salt is?

exercises.text: Я не зна́ю. А ты зна́ешь?

options: She knows where the cat is.
She doesn't know where the cat is.

exercises.prompt: What do you know, and what don't you know?

pages.title: All six, from memory
pages.intro: Every form of all three verbs, recalled. Say each one as you write it.

exercises.text: Я чита́ю. Ты ду́маешь. Мы зна́ем.

exercises.hint: We are not reading, we are thinking.

exercises.prompt: Three people, three verbs: who reads, who thinks, who knows.

units.title: In, on, and what you see
units.subtitle: в до́ме, на столе́ · ви́жу кни́гу

pages.title: In and on: где?
pages.intro: After в (in) and на (on) answering где?, most nouns end in -е.

exercises.text: Где? takes в or на, and the noun ends in -е: дом, в до́ме; стол, на столе́; ку́хня, на ку́хне. Some places take на where English says in: на ку́хне, на у́лице.

exercises.hint: The book is on the table.

options: The robot is in the house.
The robot is on the table.

exercises.prompt: Where is everything? In the house, on the table.

pages.title: In the city, in space
pages.intro: Feminine and masculine alike take -е: в го́роде, на плане́те, в ко́смосе.

exercises.text: Nearly every noun takes -е after в or на for where: в го́роде, в ко́смосе, на плане́те, в кни́ге. Nouns like ста́нция swap the final я for и: на ста́нции.

exercises.hint: The robot is on the planet.

exercises.prompt: Where are you right now? In the city, at home, in space?

pages.title: I see: ви́жу + what
pages.intro: The thing you see, read or love is the object: -а becomes -у.

exercises.text: For the object, -а becomes -у and -я becomes -ю; inanimate masculine and neuter nouns stay as they are: я ви́жу стол, я ви́жу окно́, я ви́жу кни́гу. Living masculine nouns take -а instead: брат, я ви́жу бра́та.

exercises.prompt: What do you see from where you sit?

pages.title: The station
pages.intro: A short reading: a robot, a station, the Earth in the window.

exercises.text: As the object, Земля́ becomes Зе́млю (note the stress shift) and Луна́ becomes Луну́.
Ста́нция в ко́смосе. На ста́нции живёт ро́бот. Он ви́дит Зе́млю в окне́. Ещё он ви́дит звёзды и Луну́. Ро́бот лю́бит Зе́млю.
exercises.en: A station in space. A robot lives on the station. It sees the Earth in the window. It also sees the stars and the Moon. The robot loves the Earth.

options: A robot lives on the station.
A robot works in the city.
The station is inside a robot.

exercises.hint: The robot sees the Earth in the window.

exercises.prompt: A robot looks out of a window. What does it see?

pages.title: Where: the prepositional
pages.intro: Being somewhere takes в or на and the -е ending. The accusative marks what a verb acts on. Two cells of the noun tables, side by side.

exercises.text: Где? — в до́ме, на столе́, в кни́ге: the prepositional ends in -е for all three tables (-и after -ия, -ие and for nouns in -ь: на ста́нции). The object of a verb is the accusative: for nouns I, -а → -у: Я чита́ю кни́гу.

exercises.hint: The book is on the table.

exercises.text: Где кни́га? На столе́. Что я чита́ю? Кни́гу.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: Speaking and understanding
units.subtitle: говори́ть, понима́ть, не

pages.title: Speaking: говори́ть
pages.intro: Some verbs take и where чита́ть has е: говори́шь, говори́т. Same idea, different vowel.

exercises.text: я говорю́, ты говори́шь, он говори́т, мы говори́м, вы говори́те, они́ говоря́т. The stress stays on the end throughout.

exercises.prompt: Who speaks in your home, and what do they say?

pages.title: In Russian: по-ру́сски
pages.intro: По-ру́сски means in Russian. Now you can say what you speak and what you understand.

exercises.text: You already know я не понима́ю; the full verb понима́ть (to understand) goes like чита́ть: я понима́ю, ты понима́ешь. По-ру́сски and по-англи́йски name the language.

exercises.prompt: Which languages do you speak and understand, and how well?

pages.title: Not: не and нет
pages.intro: Не negates the word after it; нет is a whole no.

exercises.text: Не sits right before the word it negates. Нет answers a question all by itself.

exercises.hint: Do you know? No, I don't.

options: They don't know who this is.
We don't know what this is.

exercises.prompt: Three things that are not so: не and нет.

pages.title: Two conjugations
pages.intro: Every present-tense verb runs on one of two sets of endings: -ешь or -ишь. Here are both tables, side by side.

exercises.text: Conjugation I has е in its endings: чита́ю, чита́ешь, чита́ет, чита́ем, чита́ете, чита́ют. Conjugation II has и: говорю́, говори́шь, говори́т, говори́м, говори́те, говоря́т. The я form and the они́ form give the rest away.

exercises.hint: Do you know where the cat is?

exercises.text: Я чита́ю, ты чита́ешь. Я говорю́, ты говори́шь.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: I think that…
pages.intro: Что joins a whole thought to the sentence: я ду́маю, что…

exercises.text: After ду́мать, знать or говори́ть, что means that, with a comma before it.

examples.en: I think that this is a fact.
He says that he doesn't know.
We know that the soup is ready.

options: Я ду́маю, что э́то не факт.

exercises.hint: I think that the soup is ready.

exercises.text: Я ду́маю, что ро́бот то́же ду́мает.

options: Do you know that this is a fact?
You think that this is not a fact.
Do you think that this is a fact?

exercises.prompt: What do you think? Two sentences with я ду́маю, что…

pages.title: Why? Because.
pages.intro: Почему́? asks why; потому́ что answers.

exercises.text: Почему́? is why?, and the answer starts with потому́ что, because. Почему́ ты так ду́маешь? is Why do you think so?

exercises.hint: I read because I love books.

exercises.text: Почему́ ты так ду́маешь? Потому́ что я зна́ю.
Почему́ ты здесь? Потому́ что я хочу́ знать.
options: Where are you? I want to know.
Why are you here? Because I know.
Why are you here? Because I want to know.

exercises.prompt: Why do you learn Russian? Answer with потому́ что.

units.title: First readings
units.subtitle: ро́бот, число́, мысль, звезда́

pages.title: Robots and rockets
pages.intro: Tiny readings from here on. Read each one for its meaning first; then say it and write it.

exercises.text: Science fiction is kind to beginners: many of its words are already familiar.
Э́то ро́бот. Он ду́мает и говори́т.

exercises.hint: The rocket is flying into space.

exercises.prompt: A robot and a rocket: a two-sentence story.

pages.title: Numbers and facts
pages.intro: Mathematics in Russian is short and exact.

exercises.text: Число́ is a number, зада́ча a problem to solve. Пра́вда is truth, or simply that's true.
Два плюс два — четы́ре. Э́то факт.
options: Two plus two is five. That's not true.
Two plus two is four. That's a fact.
Two plus four is six. That's true.

exercises.before: Два плюс два — пять? Нет, э́то
exercises.hint: Two plus two is five? No, that's not true.

exercises.prompt: A fact about numbers, in Russian.

pages.title: Thoughts
pages.intro: Мысль is thought. Philosophy, in two famous sentences.

exercises.text: Descartes and Socrates, in Russian. Ничего́ is said nichevo.

examples.ru: Я зна́ю, что ничего́ не зна́ю.
examples.en: I know that I know nothing.

exercises.text: Я зна́ю, что ничего́ не зна́ю.

exercises.hint: I know that I know nothing.

options: A fact is not a thought.
A thought is not a fact.

exercises.prompt: A thought you had today, in one sentence.

pages.title: Stars
pages.intro: One last reading, about the night sky.

exercises.text: Ночь is night, and большо́й is big. Звёзды is stars.

options: Night. Stars. Space is very big.
Morning. The sun. Space is very small.
Night. A rocket. The world is big.

exercises.prompt: The night sky, in two or three sentences.

units.title: Yesterday, today, tomorrow
units.subtitle: сего́дня, вчера́, за́втра · был, была́ · чита́л, прочита́л · бу́ду

pages.title: Today, yesterday, tomorrow
pages.intro: Time words, and the four parts of the day.

exercises.text: Сего́дня is today, вчера́ yesterday, за́втра tomorrow. For the time of day: у́тром, днём, ве́чером, но́чью.
Сего́дня я до́ма, а за́втра днём я рабо́таю.

exercises.prompt: Your day: morning, afternoon, evening. What happens when?

pages.title: Was: был, была́, бы́ло, бы́ли
pages.intro: The past tense ignores я, ты, он: it changes for gender and number, like мой.

exercises.text: The past agrees with the subject's gender: он был, она́ была́, оно́ бы́ло, они́ бы́ли. Я and ты follow the gender of the person meant.

examples.en: I was at home (said by a man).
I was at home (said by a woman).

exercises.text: Вчера́ я был до́ма, а она́ была́ там.

exercises.prompt: Where were you yesterday? Who was with you?

pages.title: Did: -л, -ла, -ли
pages.intro: Most verbs make the past by swapping -ть for -л: чита́ть, чита́л.

exercises.text: Drop -ть and add -л, -ла, -ло or -ли: чита́ть, чита́л, чита́ла, чита́ли. The stress usually stays where it was.

exercises.hint: Yesterday I (a woman) was reading a book.
He thought that it was a fact.

exercises.prompt: What did you do yesterday? Three sentences in the past.

pages.title: Finished: прочита́л
pages.intro: Most verbs come in pairs: one for the activity, one for getting it done.

exercises.text: Чита́ть is reading as an activity; прочита́ть is reading something to the end. Я чита́л кни́гу says I was reading it; я прочита́л кни́гу says I finished it.

examples.en: I read the book (to the end).
She did the work (and finished it).

exercises.before: Он до́лго чита́л кни́гу, но не
exercises.hint: He read the book for a long time, but didn't finish it.
We did the work (and finished it).

exercises.en: to do (and finish), to get done

exercises.prompt: One thing you finished yesterday, and one you only did for a while.

pages.title: A tiny story
pages.intro: A whole story in the past tense. Tap any word you want to check.

exercises.text: Вчера́ ве́чером я был до́ма. Ма́ма чита́ла кни́гу, а па́па ду́мал. Кот спал на столе́. Пото́м мы у́жинали. Бы́ло о́чень вку́сно.
exercises.en: Yesterday evening I was at home. Mom was reading a book and dad was thinking. The cat was asleep on the table. Then we had dinner. It was very tasty.

glosses.был: was (he, or a man saying I)

exercises.text: Ма́ма чита́ла кни́гу, а па́па ду́мал.
options: Dad was reading a book and mom was thinking.
Mom was reading a book and dad was thinking.
Mom and dad were reading a book.

exercises.hint: The cat was asleep on the table.

options: She was asleep on the table.

exercises.prompt: A tiny story about yesterday, in three sentences.

pages.title: What did you do?
pages.intro: Де́лать is to do. Что ты де́лал? is What did you do?

exercises.text: Что ты де́лал? asks a man, что ты де́лала? a woman, что вы де́лали? several people, or one person politely.
Что ты де́лала вчера́? Я рабо́тала, а пото́м чита́ла.

exercises.hint: And he went for a walk.

exercises.text: Вчера́ она́ рабо́тала, а он гуля́л.
options: Yesterday she worked and he went for a walk.
Yesterday he worked and she went for a walk.
Today she works and he walks.

exercises.prompt: What did you do today? Ask the same of someone.

pages.title: Tomorrow: бу́ду and прочита́ю
pages.intro: Two futures: what you will be doing, and what you will get done.

exercises.text: For an activity in the future, use бу́ду with the infinitive: за́втра я бу́ду чита́ть. Бу́ду goes бу́ду, бу́дешь, бу́дет, бу́дем, бу́дете, бу́дут. A finishing verb with present endings is already future: я прочита́ю, I will read it through.
Что ты бу́дешь де́лать за́втра? Я бу́ду чита́ть.

exercises.prompt: What will you do tomorrow, and what will you get done?

pages.title: The past-tense table
pages.intro: One form per gender and one plural, whoever is speaking. Here is the table, and the verbs that move their stress.

exercises.text: Drop -ть, add -л, -ла, -ло, -ли: чита́л, чита́ла, чита́ло, чита́ли. The form agrees with the subject's gender or number, not its person: я чита́л, я чита́ла, мы чита́ли. быть moves its stress: был, была́, бы́ло, бы́ли.

exercises.hint: They thought for a long time.

exercises.text: Был, была́, бы́ло, бы́ли. Чита́л, чита́ла, чита́ло, чита́ли.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: Going places
units.subtitle: идти́, ходи́ть, е́хать

pages.title: On foot: идти́
pages.intro: Идти́ is going on foot, right now, in one direction.

exercises.text: я иду́, ты идёшь, он идёт, мы идём, вы идёте, они́ иду́т. Куда́? asks where to; the answer is в or на with the object form (в парк, на рабо́ту), or simply домо́й.
Куда́ вы идёте? Мы идём на рабо́ту.

exercises.hint: I am going to the park (where to?).

exercises.prompt: Where are you going right now, and where is someone else going?

pages.title: Again and again; by car or train
pages.intro: Ходи́ть is going on foot regularly. Е́хать is going by transport.

exercises.text: Ходи́ть is going on foot again and again: я хожу́ в парк ка́ждый день. Е́хать is going by car, bus or train: я е́ду, ты е́дешь.

examples.en: I'm going home (by car, bus or train).

exercises.hint: Every day I go to the park.
Tomorrow we are going to the city (by car, bus or train).

exercises.text: Он хо́дит в парк ка́ждый день.
Он хо́дит на рабо́ту ка́ждый день.
options: He is going to work today.
He goes to work every day.

exercises.prompt: Where do you go every day, and how do you get there?

pages.title: Where did you go?
pages.intro: Motion in the past, and a short day in the life.

exercises.text: In the past идти́ becomes шёл, шла, шли, and е́хать becomes е́хал. Ходи́л, from ходи́ть, means went and came back.

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the park (man).

exercises.text: Вчера́ у́тром я ходи́ла в парк. Там бы́ло ти́хо. Пото́м я рабо́тала. Ве́чером мы бы́ли до́ма и чита́ли. За́втра я опя́ть иду́ в парк.
exercises.en: Yesterday morning I went to the park. It was quiet there. Then I worked. In the evening we were at home and read. Tomorrow I'm going to the park again.

glosses.ходила: went and came back (she, or a woman saying I)

options: Then I went to work by bus.

exercises.hint: Yesterday I (a woman) went to the park.

exercises.prompt: Where did you go today, and how?

pages.title: Where to: the accusative of direction
pages.intro: Куда́? takes the same в and на — with the accusative. The table of идти́ and е́хать goes with it.

exercises.text: Where something is: в го́роде (prepositional). Where it is going: в го́род (accusative). Nouns II that are things keep their dictionary form as the accusative, so the preposition does all the work: в парк, but в па́рке.

exercises.hint: We are going to the city.
We are going to the park.

exercises.text: Я иду́ в парк, а ты идёшь домо́й.
Куда́ ты идёшь? В го́род. Где ты живёшь? В го́роде.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: A signal from space
units.subtitle: a short story in four parts

pages.title: The station Zvezda
pages.intro: Part one. Read it through for the gist, tapping what you need; then listen to it whole.

exercises.text: Ста́нция «Звезда́» лети́т вокру́г Земли́. На ста́нции рабо́тает Ми́ра. Ми́ра — ро́бот. Ка́ждое у́тро она́ смо́трит на звёзды. Сего́дня она́ слы́шит стра́нный сигна́л.
exercises.en: The station Zvezda (Star) flies around the Earth. Mira works on the station. Mira is a robot. Every morning she looks at the stars. Today she hears a strange signal.

glosses.на: on; here: at (смотрит на: looks at)

options: Today she sends a strange signal.
Yesterday she heard a strange signal.
Today she hears a strange signal.

exercises.text: Ка́ждое у́тро она́ смо́трит на звёзды.

exercises.prompt: Describe a station in space in three sentences.

pages.title: Numbers in the noise
pages.intro: Part two. Mira listens closely.

exercises.text: Ми́ра слу́шает сигна́л. Э́то не шум: в сигна́ле есть чи́сла. Два, три, пять, семь, оди́ннадцать… Ми́ра ду́мает: «Э́то просты́е чи́сла. Зна́чит, там кто́-то есть».
exercises.en: Mira listens to the signal. It isn't noise: there are numbers in the signal. Two, three, five, seven, eleven… Mira thinks: “These are prime numbers. So someone is out there.”

exercises.text: Э́то не шум: в сигна́ле есть чи́сла.

exercises.prompt: You hear numbers in the noise. Write what they are and what you think.

pages.title: The answer
pages.intro: Part three. Mira replies, and waits.

exercises.text: Ми́ра пи́шет отве́т: два, три, пять, семь, оди́ннадцать, трина́дцать. Она́ посыла́ет его́ к звёздам. Пото́м она́ ждёт. Оди́н день, два дня, неде́лю. Ко́смос молчи́т.
exercises.en: Mira writes an answer: two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen. She sends it to the stars. Then she waits. One day, two days, a week. Space is silent.

exercises.prompt: Write a short message to send into space.

pages.title: Hello
pages.intro: Part four. A month later.

exercises.text: Че́рез ме́сяц прихо́дит но́вый сигна́л. В нём одно́ сло́во: «Приве́т». Ми́ра не зна́ет, кто э́то. Но тепе́рь она́ зна́ет: мы не одни́.
exercises.en: A month later a new signal arrives. It has one word in it: “Hello.” Mira doesn't know who it is. But now she knows: we are not alone.

glosses.через: after, in (через месяц: a month later)

options: Mira doesn't know who it is.

exercises.hint: But now she knows: we are not alone.

exercises.prompt: A month later: what happened? Two or three sentences.

units.title: Mathematics
units.subtitle: чи́сла до ста · е́сли… то… · существу́ет

pages.title: Numbers to a hundred
pages.intro: Tens, and how to build every number up to сто.

exercises.text: Twenty to ninety: два́дцать, три́дцать, со́рок, пятьдеся́т, шестьдеся́т, се́мьдесят, во́семьдесят, девяно́сто; a hundred is сто. Join the rest: два́дцать оди́н, со́рок пять.
Два́дцать, три́дцать, со́рок, пятьдеся́т, шестьдеся́т, се́мьдесят, во́семьдесят, девяно́сто, сто.

options: Ninety plus ten is a hundred.

exercises.prompt: Three numbers over twenty, written out, with a sum.

pages.title: Even, odd, if… then
pages.intro: Mathematical Russian is built from a handful of words.

exercises.text: Чётное число́ is an even number, нечётное an odd one. Е́сли A, то B is if A, then B.

examples.ru: Е́сли число́ чётное, то оно́ де́лится на два.
examples.en: If a number is even, then it is divisible by two.

exercises.after: число́ чётное, то оно́ де́лится на два.
exercises.hint: If a number is even, then it is divisible by two.

exercises.text: Е́сли число́ чётное, то оно́ де́лится на два.
Е́сли пять — чётное число́, то я ро́бот.
options: Five is an even number, so I am a robot.
If I am a robot, then five is even.
If five is an even number, then I am a robot.

exercises.prompt: An even number, an odd number, and an if-then sentence.

pages.title: For every, there exists
pages.intro: The two quantifiers: для любо́го and существу́ет.

exercises.text: Для любо́го числа́ is for any number; существу́ет число́ is there exists a number.

examples.ru: Для любо́го числа́ существу́ет бо́льшее число́.
examples.en: For any number there exists a bigger number.

exercises.hint: For any number there exists a bigger number.

exercises.text: Для любо́го числа́ существу́ет бо́льшее число́.

options: There exists an even prime number: two.

exercises.prompt: One sentence with для любо́го and one with существу́ет.

pages.title: Before the proof
pages.intro: The three phrases the proof is built from, one clause at a time.

exercises.text: Де́лится на два means is divisible by two. Кото́рое joins a description to a neuter noun: число́, кото́рое де́лится на два. Два, умно́женное на три is two multiplied by three.

examples.ru: Шесть — э́то два, умно́женное на три.
examples.en: Six is two multiplied by three.

examples.ru: Чётное число́ — э́то число́, кото́рое де́лится на два.
examples.en: An even number is a number that is divisible by two.
Five is a whole number (an integer).

options: Nine is not divisible by two.
Two is not divisible by nine.

exercises.hint: Eight is two multiplied by four.

exercises.text: Чётное число́ — э́то число́, кото́рое де́лится на два.

exercises.before: Де́вять — нечётное число́, потому́ что оно́ не
exercises.hint: Nine is odd, because it is not divisible by two.

exercises.prompt: State a tiny mathematical claim in one clause.

pages.title: A tiny proof
pages.intro: Your first Russian proof: the sum of two even numbers is even.

exercises.text: Теоре́ма: су́мма двух чётных чи́сел — чётное число́. Доказа́тельство. Чётное число́ — э́то число́, кото́рое де́лится на два. Возьмём два чётных числа́. Ка́ждое из них — два, умно́женное на це́лое число́. Их су́мма — два, умно́женное на су́мму э́тих це́лых чи́сел. Зна́чит, су́мма то́же де́лится на два, то есть она́ чётная. Что и тре́бовалось доказа́ть.
exercises.en: Theorem: the sum of two even numbers is an even number. Proof. An even number is a number that is divisible by two. Take two even numbers. Each of them is two multiplied by a whole number. Their sum is two multiplied by the sum of those whole numbers. So the sum is also divisible by two, that is, it is even. Which was to be proved.

glosses.что: what; here: which (что и требовалось доказать: Q.E.D.)

exercises.text: Су́мма двух чётных чи́сел — чётное число́.
options: The sum of two odd numbers is an odd number.
The product of two even numbers is odd.
The sum of two even numbers is an even number.

exercises.hint: An even number is divisible by two.

exercises.text: Су́мма двух чётных чи́сел — чётное число́.

exercises.prompt: Your own two-line proof of something simple.

pages.title: The genitive: нет, of, and after numbers
pages.intro: One case, three jobs: what is missing, what something is of, and what comes after a number.

exercises.text: Nouns II take -а (-я) in the genitive singular: нет хле́ба, для любо́го числа́. Nouns I take -ы (-и): нет кни́ги. In the plural, nouns I and neuter nouns II lose their ending — книг, чи́сел — and masculine nouns take -ов: пять столо́в.
Су́мма двух чётных чи́сел — чётное число́.
Оди́н стол, два стола́, пять столо́в.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: Philosophy
units.subtitle: Socrates, Tyutchev, Bulgakov

pages.title: A dialogue
pages.intro: Socrates asks a student a simple question that is not simple.

exercises.text:
— Что тако́е справедли́вость? — спра́шивает Сокра́т.
— Э́то когда́ ка́ждый получа́ет то, чего́ заслу́живает, — отвеча́ет учени́к.
— А кто зна́ет, чего́ заслу́живает ка́ждый?
— Наве́рное, му́дрый челове́к.
— Зна́чит, что́бы быть справедли́вым, ну́жно быть му́дрым?
— Да, ка́жется, так.
— Тогда́ снача́ла ну́жно узна́ть, что тако́е му́дрость.
exercises.en: “What is justice?” asks Socrates. “It's when everyone gets what they deserve,” answers the student. “And who knows what everyone deserves?” “A wise person, probably.” “So to be just, one has to be wise?” “Yes, it seems so.” “Then first we need to find out what wisdom is.”

exercises.text: Что́бы быть справедли́вым, ну́жно быть му́дрым.
options: To be wise, one has to be just.
A just person is never wise.
To be just, one has to be wise.

exercises.text: Что́бы быть справедли́вым, ну́жно быть му́дрым.

exercises.prompt: A question that is not simple, and a first attempt at an answer.

pages.title: Real words: Tyutchev and Bulgakov
pages.intro: An excursion, not a test: four lines by Fyodor Tyutchev (1866) about what reason cannot measure, and one line from Bulgakov. Short poems are harder than they look.

exercises.text:
Э́то стихи́ Фёдора Тю́тчева.
Умо́м Росси́ю не поня́ть,
Арши́ном о́бщим не изме́рить:
У ней осо́бенная стать —
В Росси́ю мо́жно то́лько ве́рить.
exercises.en: These are verses by Fyodor Tyutchev. Russia cannot be understood with the mind, nor measured with a common yardstick: she has a special character — one can only believe in Russia.

glosses.аршином: with an arshin (an old Russian measuring rod)
glosses.у: at, by (у ней, old-style: she has)

options: Russia can be understood with the mind.
Russia cannot be understood with the mind.
The mind does not understand Russian.

exercises.hint: One can only believe in Russia.

exercises.text: Булга́ков, «Ма́стер и Маргари́та»: Ру́кописи не горя́т. Manuscripts don't burn.

exercises.prompt: Something you know, and something you don't, in your own words.

units.title: Word families
units.subtitle: ко́рни · приста́вки · су́ффиксы · Greek and Latin

pages.title: One root, many words: пис-
pages.intro: Russian builds its words from a few hundred roots. Learn the root and its prefixes and suffixes, and whole families come at once.

exercises.text: The root пис- (пиш- before some endings) means write: писа́ть to write, письмо́ a letter, писа́тель a writer, написа́ть to write and finish. Prefixes and suffixes do the rest.

exercises.en: I want to write a letter.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: Reading and counting: чит-
pages.intro: One root for reading and counting, and число́ grows from it too.

exercises.text: Чита́ть and счита́ть, to count, share one root: чит-, чт-, чёт-. So do число́, a number, and чётное, even. A reader is чита́тель; reading is чте́ние.

exercises.hint: The reader reads, and the writer writes.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: In, out, across: prefixes on ход-
pages.intro: Ходи́ть and идти́ share the root ход-. A prefix gives the direction, and a noun falls out.

exercises.text: В- is in, вы- is out, пере- is across. On the root ход-, go: вход the way in, вы́ход the way out, перехо́д a crossing.

exercises.en: Where is the entrance to the park?

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: Suffixes: -тель, -ник, -ость, -ние
pages.intro: A suffix says what kind of word you have: a person, a quality, an activity.

exercises.text: -тель and -ник make a person: учи́тель teacher, учени́к pupil, рабо́тник worker. -ость makes a quality: му́дрость wisdom. -ние makes an activity: зна́ние knowledge.

exercises.hint: A wise person knows what wisdom is.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: Greek you already know
pages.intro: Greek came into Russian sound by sound. Read these as Greek and they are yours.

exercises.text: Th is т (тео́рия), ph is ф (филосо́фия), -y is -ия, and -ics is -ика (ло́гика, матема́тика). The pieces are Greek too: фило- love, -со́фия wisdom, гео- earth, -ме́трия measuring.

exercises.hint: This is not a theory, it is a fact.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

pages.title: Latin you already know
pages.intro: Latin came the same way, with its own endings.

exercises.text: -tion is -ция (фу́нкция), -ure is -ура (структу́ра), -ment is -мент (аргуме́нт, элеме́нт). Abstractio is абстра́кция; informatio, информа́ция.

exercises.hint: Two is an element, not a system.

exercises.prompt: Two sentences of your own, with words from this page.

units.title: Cases as a system
units.subtitle: паде́ж: роди́тельный, да́тельный, твори́тельный, предло́жный

pages.title: Genitive: чего́ нет
pages.intro: You know нет хле́ба. The same ending serves у, из, по́сле, мно́го and ма́ло: one case, five uses.

exercises.text: The genitive answers чего́? and кого́?. Нет, у, из and по́сле take it, and so do мно́го and ма́ло: a masculine noun adds -а, a feminine -а becomes -ы or -и, and a plural often loses its ending altogether. Вре́мя, time, is irregular: learn нет вре́мени as one piece.

examples.en: at my brother's; my brother has
at my sister's; my sister has

exercises.text: По́сле обе́да у меня́ есть вре́мя, а у бра́та вре́мени нет. У сестры́ мно́го рабо́ты.
У сестры́ мно́го книг, а у бра́та ма́ло.
options: My sister has many books, and my brother few.
My sister has few books, and my brother many.
My sister and brother have no books.

exercises.prompt: What do you have little of, and a lot of? Where are you from? Three sentences in the genitive.

pages.title: Dative: кому́?
pages.intro: The person something goes to, and two idioms that live in this case: age and liking.

exercises.text: The dative answers кому́?: the person something goes to. Мне, тебе́, ему́, ей, нам, вам, им are its pronouns; a masculine noun adds -у (бра́ту), a feminine one swaps -а for -е (сестре́).

examples.en: I am writing a letter to my sister.

exercises.text: Age and liking are dative too: Мне три́дцать лет, I am thirty; мне нра́вится, I like it, literally it pleases me.

exercises.hint: I am writing a letter to my brother.

exercises.text: Ско́лько тебе́ лет? Мне со́рок лет. Вам нра́вится матема́тика? Да, нам нра́вится. А ему́ нет.

exercises.prompt: Who do you write to, and what do you like? Say your age.

pages.title: Instrumental: с кем? чем?
pages.intro: Who with, by what means, and what someone is or becomes.

exercises.text: The instrumental answers с кем? and чем?: who with, and by what means. A masculine noun adds -ом (с бра́том), a feminine one -ой (с сестро́й); the pronouns are со мной, с тобо́й, с ним, с ней, с на́ми, с ва́ми, с ни́ми.
Быть and стать, to become, take it too: он был учи́телем, она́ ста́ла писа́телем.

exercises.hint: I'm going to the park with my brother.

exercises.text: Э́то моя́ ру́чка. Я пишу́ письмо́ ру́чкой. Со мной брат, с тобо́й сестра́.

options: I want to become a teacher.
I want to be with a teacher.

exercises.prompt: Who did you spend today with, and what do you want to become?

pages.title: Where, or where to: в and на
pages.intro: The same two prepositions, two cases: where something is, and where it is going. And о, about.

exercises.text: В and на take two cases: где? takes the prepositional (-е), куда́? the accusative: plain for masculine and neuter things, -у for feminine ones (в го́род, на рабо́ту). О, about, also takes the prepositional: о кни́ге, о тебе́.

examples.ru: Я на рабо́те. Я иду́ на рабо́ту.
examples.en: I am at work. I am going to work.

examples.ru: Кот на столе́. Кот идёт на стол.
examples.en: The cat is on the table. The cat is getting onto the table.
goes, is going (he, she, it; on foot)

examples.ru: Я в го́роде. Я е́ду в го́род.
examples.en: I'm in the city. I'm going to the city.

exercises.hint: The book is on the table.

exercises.text: Где ты? На рабо́те. Куда́ ты идёшь? На рабо́ту. Кот идёт на стол. Я ду́маю о бра́те.

options: She is going to her brother.
She is thinking about her brother.

exercises.prompt: Where is each thing in your room, and where is it going? Then: what are you thinking about?

pages.title: Six cases, one story
pages.intro: The table has names now. Read a day that uses every row of it.

exercises.text: The six cases have names: имени́тельный (кто? что?), роди́тельный (кого́? чего́?), да́тельный (кому́?), вини́тельный (кого́? что?, the object — like роди́тельный for living masculine nouns), твори́тельный (кем? чем?), предло́жный (о ком? о чём?, где?). A grammar table lists them in this order.

Вчера́ по́сле рабо́ты я ходи́ла в го́род с сестро́й. У сестры́ мно́го книг, а у меня́ ма́ло вре́мени. В го́роде мы бы́ли до́лго. Пото́м я написа́ла письмо́ бра́ту о го́роде и о сестре́. Брат отве́тил: «Мне нра́вится э́то письмо́».
exercises.en: Yesterday after work I went to the city with my sister. My sister has many books, and I have little time. We were in the city a long time. Then I wrote a letter to my brother about the city and about my sister. My brother answered: “I like this letter.”

glosses.ходила: went and came back (a woman saying I)
glosses.городе: city (в городе: in the city; о городе: about the city)

exercises.text: Я написа́ла письмо́ бра́ту о го́роде.
options: I wrote a letter to my sister about my brother.
I wrote a letter to my brother about the city.
My brother wrote me a letter about the city.

exercises.hint: I went to the city with my sister.

exercises.text: Я написа́ла письмо́ бра́ту о го́роде.
Роди́тельный паде́ж, да́тельный паде́ж, вини́тельный паде́ж, твори́тельный паде́ж, предло́жный паде́ж.

exercises.prompt: A day of yours that uses every case: with whom, to whom, about what.

units.title: Aspect
units.subtitle: вид: чита́ть — прочита́ть · бу́ду чита́ть — прочита́ю · скажи́!

pages.title: Two verbs for one
pages.intro: Nearly every verb comes as a pair. Here are the pairs for the verbs you already have.

exercises.text: The imperfective names the activity or a repeated act; the perfective names one completed result. You know чита́ть / прочита́ть and де́лать / сде́лать; here are the rest of your verbs.

examples.en: to write — to write and finish
to think — to think for a moment, think it over
to see — to catch sight of
to wait — to wait a bit

exercises.hint: I want to find out who this is.
I understand what you want to say.

exercises.text: Чита́ть — прочита́ть, писа́ть — написа́ть, говори́ть — сказа́ть, ждать — подожда́ть, ви́деть — уви́деть. Он хо́чет поня́ть.
Она́ хо́чет поня́ть, а не то́лько знать.
options: She wants to know, not just to understand.
She wants to understand, not just to know.

exercises.prompt: Three things you want to find out, say or understand this week.

pages.title: Process or result: the past
pages.intro: Я писа́л письмо́ is the evening; я написа́л письмо́ is the letter in the envelope.

exercises.text: In the past, the imperfective says what was going on, the perfective what got done. Both are needed in one story: the long evening, then the result.

examples.ru: Я до́лго писа́л письмо́ и наконе́ц написа́л.
examples.en: I wrote the letter for a long time and finally finished it.

examples.ru: Она́ говори́ла до́лго, а пото́м сказа́ла: «Да».
examples.en: She talked for a long time, and then said: “Yes.”

examples.ru: Мы жда́ли час и наконе́ц уви́дели раке́ту.
examples.en: We waited an hour and finally saw the rocket.
I thought a moment and understood.

exercises.hint: He thought for a long time and finally understood.
Yesterday I was writing a letter, but didn't finish it.

exercises.text: Мы жда́ли и наконе́ц уви́дели звезду́.
Я поду́мал и по́нял. Она́ до́лго говори́ла и наконе́ц сказа́ла: «Да».
Она́ чита́ла кни́гу, но не прочита́ла.
options: She was reading the book but didn't finish it.

exercises.prompt: Yesterday: one thing you did for a long time, one you finished.

pages.title: Two futures
pages.intro: Бу́ду + infinitive for an activity; the perfective with present endings for a result.

exercises.text: The imperfective future is бу́ду + infinitive: an activity. The perfective future is just the perfective verb with present endings: a result you expect.

examples.en: I will write the letter (and finish).

exercises.hint: Tomorrow I will write (and finish) a letter to my sister.

exercises.text: Я бу́ду чита́ть, и я прочита́ю. Вы уви́дите: он сде́лает, а я поду́маю.

options: You will see: he will get it done.
You will see him doing it.

exercises.prompt: Tomorrow: what you will be doing, and what you will get done.

pages.title: Tell me: imperatives
pages.intro: Asking, telling, warning. The imperative comes straight from the ты-form.

exercises.text: The imperative comes from the ты-form: чита́й, скажи́, напиши́, подожди́, слу́шай, смотри́. Add -те for вы or for politeness: скажи́те, пожа́луйста. A perfective asks for one act; a negative request is usually imperfective: не говори́.

exercises.hint: Tell me, please, where is the exit?

exercises.text: Скажи́ мне. Подожди́. Смотри́, э́то раке́та! Чита́й ме́дленно, не говори́ бы́стро.
Чита́й ме́дленно и не говори́ бы́стро.
options: Read fast and don't talk slowly.
Read slowly and don't talk fast.

exercises.prompt: Three requests to someone at home: one polite, one urgent, one a warning.

units.title: Numbers and things
units.subtitle: два стола́, пять столо́в · кото́рый час? · ско́лько сто́ит?

pages.title: One, two, five: the noun changes
pages.intro: After оди́н, after два, after пять: three shapes of the same noun.

exercises.text: After оди́н the noun is plain (оди́н стол); after два, три, четы́ре it takes the genitive singular (два стола́, две кни́ги); after пять and up, the genitive plural (пять столо́в, пять книг). Два becomes две with a feminine noun.

examples.ru: оди́н стол, два стола́, пять столо́в
examples.en: one table, two tables, five tables

examples.ru: одна́ кни́га, две кни́ги, пять книг
examples.en: one book, two books, five books

examples.ru: одно́ окно́, два окна́, пять о́кон
examples.en: one window, two windows, five windows

examples.ru: оди́н год, два го́да, пять лет
examples.en: one year, two years, five years

exercises.hint: There are five windows in the house.

exercises.text: Оди́н стол, два стола́, пять столо́в. Одна́ кни́га, две кни́ги, пять книг. Одно́ окно́, два окна́, пять о́кон. Оди́н год, два го́да, пять лет.

exercises.prompt: Count what is in your kitchen: one, two, five of something.

pages.title: What time is it?
pages.intro: Hours count like tables: час, два часа́, пять часо́в.

exercises.text: Кото́рый час? or Ско́лько вре́мени? asks the time. Час is an hour and one o'clock: два часа́, пять часо́в; в три часа́ is at three. Утра́ and ве́чера tell morning from evening: в семь часо́в утра́.
Кото́рый час? Сейча́с два часа́. За́втрак в во́семь часо́в утра́, у́жин в семь часо́в ве́чера.

options: Breakfast is at eight in the morning.
Breakfast is at eight in the evening.

exercises.prompt: Your day in hours: when you get up, eat, work, sleep.

pages.title: Days and dates
pages.intro: The week, and the date as a neuter ordinal.

exercises.text: The week: понеде́льник, вто́рник, среда́, четве́рг, пя́тница, суббо́та, воскресе́нье. On a day is в + accusative: в понеде́льник, в сре́ду, в пя́тницу. Dates use the neuter ordinal: пе́рвое ма́я, the first of May.

examples.ru: янва́рь, февра́ль, март, апре́ль, май, ию́нь
examples.en: January, February, March, April, May, June

examples.ru: ию́ль, а́вгуст, сентя́брь, октя́брь, ноя́брь, дека́брь
examples.en: July, August, September, October, November, December

exercises.hint: We're going to the city on Saturday.

exercises.text: В пя́тницу я рабо́таю, в суббо́ту — нет.

Како́й сего́дня день? Понеде́льник. Понеде́льник, вто́рник, среда́, четве́рг, пя́тница, суббо́та, воскресе́нье. Янва́рь, февра́ль, март, апре́ль, май, ию́нь, ию́ль, а́вгуст, сентя́брь, октя́брь, ноя́брь, дека́брь. Како́е сего́дня число́? Пе́рвое ма́я, второ́е, тре́тье.

options: What's the date today? The third of May.
What time is it? Three o'clock.

exercises.prompt: What day and date is it, and what do you do on which days?

pages.title: Prices and quantities
pages.intro: How much is it, and how much of it: сто́ит, рубли́, and the genitive again.

exercises.text: Ско́лько сто́ит? asks a price: сто́ит for one thing, сто́ят for several. Money counts like everything else: оди́н рубль, два рубля́, пять рубле́й. Quantities take the genitive: буты́лка молока́, килогра́мм сы́ра, литр воды́.

exercises.hint: The soup costs a hundred roubles.
A kilogram of cheese is expensive.

exercises.text: Ско́лько сто́ит литр воды́? Два́дцать рубле́й. Э́то дёшево. А кни́ги сто́ят до́рого.
Кни́ги сто́ят до́рого, а хлеб — дёшево.
options: Books are expensive, but bread is cheap.
Books are cheap, but bread is expensive.
Books and bread cost the same.

exercises.prompt: Three things you bought, with their prices.

pages.title: A menu and a recipe
pages.intro: Two texts you will meet in any kitchen: prices, and instructions in the polite imperative.

exercises.text: Меню́. За́втрак: ка́ша с молоко́м — сто два́дцать рубле́й, чай и́ли ко́фе — шестьдеся́т рубле́й. Обе́д: суп — две́сти рубле́й, хлеб — три́дцать. У́жин: щи, сыр и чай — три́ста рубле́й.
exercises.en: Menu. Breakfast: porridge with milk, 120 roubles; tea or coffee, 60 roubles. Lunch: soup, 200 roubles; bread, 30. Dinner: cabbage soup, cheese and tea, 300 roubles.

exercises.text: Ка́ша. Возьми́те рис, молоко́ и соль. Нале́йте молоко́ в кастрю́лю. Вари́те де́сять мину́т. Пото́м доба́вьте са́хар. Прия́тного аппети́та!
exercises.en: Porridge. Take rice, milk and salt. Pour the milk into a saucepan. Cook for ten minutes. Then add sugar. Enjoy your meal!

exercises.text: Чай и́ли ко́фе? Ко́фе с молоко́м, пожа́луйста. Вари́те де́сять мину́т.

exercises.prompt: A recipe for something you make, in the polite imperative.

units.title: Describing and comparing
units.subtitle: лу́чше, ху́же · прав, ну́жен · э́тот, тот · кото́рый

pages.title: More and less
pages.intro: Comparing two things, and naming the most.

exercises.text: Compare with -ее and чем: интере́снее, чем, more interesting than. A few comparatives are irregular and very common: бо́льше more, ме́ньше less, лу́чше better, ху́же worse, ста́рше older, моло́же younger. Са́мый makes the superlative: са́мая интере́сная кни́га.

examples.en: This book is more interesting than the film.
My brother is older, my sister younger.

exercises.hint: Mathematics is more interesting than a film.
My brother is older than me.

exercises.text: Бо́льше, ме́ньше, лу́чше, ху́же, ста́рше, моло́же. Ва́жный, тру́дный, лёгкий.

options: This is a more interesting book.
This is the most interesting book.

exercises.prompt: Compare two books, two cities or two foods.

pages.title: Short forms: прав, ну́жен, до́лжен
pages.intro: Adjectives have a short form used only as a predicate; here are the ones you will hear most. Adverbs end in -о.

exercises.text: Some adjectives have a short form used only as a predicate: ты прав / ты права́, you are right; я согла́сен / согла́сна, I agree; мне ну́жен / нужна́ / ну́жно, I need; я до́лжен / должна́, I must. Adverbs end in -о and double as it is…: тру́дно, легко́, ва́жно, интере́сно.

exercises.hint: You're right (to a man), this is important.

exercises.text: Э́то тру́дно, но интере́сно. А э́то легко́ и ва́жно. Я согла́сен, и я до́лжен идти́.

options: He has a lot of time.

exercises.prompt: What do you need, and what must you do today?

pages.title: This and that: э́тот, тот
pages.intro: Э́то alone points; before a noun it agrees. Тот is the one further away.

exercises.text: Э́то alone points: э́то кни́га, this is a book. Before a noun it agrees: э́тот стол, э́та кни́га, э́то окно́, э́ти кни́ги. Тот, та, то, те is that one, further away.

examples.en: This tea is better than that one.

exercises.hint: This book is mine, and that one is yours.

exercises.text: Э́тот стол но́вый, а тот ста́рый.
Э́тот, э́та, э́то, э́ти. Тот, та, то, те.

options: Those books are more interesting than these.
These books are the most interesting.
These books are more interesting than those.

exercises.text: э́тот — тот, э́та — та, э́ти — те

exercises.prompt: This thing and that thing: compare what is near you with what is across the room.

pages.title: Which: кото́рый
pages.intro: The word that joins a clause to a noun: the gateway to real sentences.

exercises.text: Кото́рый joins a clause to a noun, like which or who. It agrees with the noun in gender and number, and takes the case its own clause needs: челове́к, кото́рый чита́ет; кни́га, кото́рую я чита́ю; го́род, в кото́ром я живу́.

examples.en: the book that I am reading
I see a person who is waiting.

exercises.hint: This is the book that I love.
This is the city where my brother lives.

exercises.text: Кни́га, кото́рую я чита́ю, о ко́смосе.
Я зна́ю челове́ка, кото́рый живёт на ста́нции.
options: I know a station where a person lives.
A person knows that I live on the station.
I know a person who lives on the station.

exercises.prompt: Three sentences with кото́рый about people and things you know.

pages.title: Reading with кото́рый
pages.intro: Mira again, in sentences with clauses inside them.

exercises.text: Ми́ра — ро́бот, кото́рый живёт на ста́нции. Ста́нция, на кото́рой она́ рабо́тает, лети́т вокру́г Земли́. Ка́ждое у́тро Ми́ра чита́ет кни́ги, кото́рые ей нра́вятся. Са́мая интере́сная кни́га — та, в кото́рой есть зада́чи. Э́ти зада́чи трудне́е, чем те, кото́рые она́ реша́ла вчера́.
exercises.en: Mira is a robot who lives on the station. The station she works on flies around the Earth. Every morning Mira reads books that she likes. The most interesting book is the one with problems in it. These problems are harder than the ones she solved yesterday.

glosses.которой: which (на которой: on which; в которой: in which)

options: Those problems are harder than these.
These problems are harder than those.

exercises.hint: Mira is a robot who lives on the station.
The most interesting book is the one with problems in it.

exercises.text: Ста́нция, на кото́рой она́ рабо́тает, лети́т вокру́г Земли́.

exercises.prompt: Describe someone you know in sentences with clauses inside them.

units.title: The machinery of written Russian
units.subtitle: -ся · чита́ющий, прочита́в · же, ведь · что́бы

pages.title: Verbs with -ся
pages.intro: A tail that turns the verb back on its subject, or just marks a verb with no object.

exercises.text: -ся on the end of a verb turns it back on its subject, or marks a verb that takes no object: учи́ться to study, называ́ться to be called, находи́ться to be located, начина́ться to begin, конча́ться to end. After a vowel it is -сь: учу́сь.

examples.en: I am learning to read Russian.

exercises.hint: The lesson begins at eight o'clock.

exercises.text: Как э́то называ́ется? Где э́то нахо́дится? Когда́ э́то начина́ется и конча́ется? Мне ка́жется, в де́вять.

options: It seems to me the lesson is beginning.
It seems to me the lesson is ending.
I know the lesson is over.

exercises.prompt: What are you learning, when does your day begin and end, and what is this thing called?

pages.title: Verbs dressed as adjectives
pages.intro: Participles and gerunds: read who did what, and when. Leave production for later.

exercises.text: A participle is a verb wearing an adjective ending. -ущий/-ющий/-ащий/-ящий is doing: чита́ющий, the one who is reading; -вший did: прочита́вший; -нный and -тый was done: напи́санный, written, откры́тый, open. A gerund is a verb used as an adverb: чита́я, while reading; прочита́в, having read.

examples.en: a robot living on the station
the one having read the book
While reading the letter, she was silent.

options: This is a letter written by my brother.
This is a letter my brother is writing.
This is a letter to my brother.
a person who has finished reading
someone who is still reading the book
someone who has not read the book
someone who has finished the book
a letter that writes and a window that opens something
a letter to write and a window to close
a written letter and an open window
Having read the letter, she spoke.
While reading the letter, she was silent.
She was reading a letter about silence.
Before reading the book, I thought.
Having finished the book, I thought.
While still reading the book, I thought.

exercises.text: Чита́ющий, прочита́вший, живу́щий. Напи́санный, откры́тый. Чита́я, она́ молча́ла. Прочита́в, она́ поду́мала.

exercises.prompt: What did you read today? Write a few words of your own; simple sentences are enough.

pages.title: Word order and emphasis
pages.intro: The cases carry the roles, so the order carries the emphasis: the important word goes last.

exercises.text: Russian word order is free because the cases carry the roles; the new or important word goes last. Ма́ма чита́ет кни́гу answers what is mom doing, Кни́гу чита́ет ма́ма answers who is reading the book. Little words add emphasis: же (precisely), ведь (after all), да́же (even), то́лько (only).

examples.en: It's mom who is reading the book.

exercises.hint: You know where the salt is, after all.
I did say so: it's a fact!

exercises.text: Кни́гу чита́ет ма́ма. Ма́ма чита́ет кни́гу. Ма́ма кни́гу чита́ет.
Письмо́ написа́л брат, а не сестра́.
options: My brother wrote a letter to my sister.
It was my brother who wrote the letter, not my sister.
My sister wrote the letter, not my brother.

exercises.prompt: Say who did what, three ways, moving the emphasis each time.

pages.title: That, which, what: clause words
pages.intro: Что for a fact, что́бы for a purpose or a wish, то, что for the thing that.

exercises.text: Что joins a fact: я зна́ю, что. Что́бы joins a purpose or a wish: я чита́ю, что́бы знать; я хочу́, что́бы ты знал. То, что is the thing that, тот, кто the one who, and де́ло в том, что means the point is that.

examples.ru: Я зна́ю то, что ты зна́ешь.

examples.en: The one who waits will see.
I read in order to know.

examples.ru: Де́ло в том, что у меня́ нет вре́мени.
examples.en: The thing is, I have no time.

exercises.hint: I study in order to read Russian.
The one who waits will see (two words: that one, who).

exercises.text: Де́ло в том, что я не зна́ю.
Я хочу́, что́бы ты по́нял то, что я зна́ю. Е́сли бы я знал!
Е́сли бы у меня́ бы́ло вре́мя!
что — что́бы — то, что — тот, кто

exercises.prompt: Why do you read? Two sentences with что́бы, and one with де́ло в том, что.

pages.title: Science fiction: two scenes
pages.intro: Two short originals in the manner of the Russian classics of the genre: a city of glass, and a station on Mars.

exercises.text: Я живу́ в го́роде из стекла́. Ка́ждое у́тро в семь часо́в мы все встаём, и ка́ждый ве́чер в де́сять мы все спим. Стена́, отделя́ющая нас от ле́са, то́же из стекла́. Сего́дня я уви́дел за стено́й челове́ка, кото́рый не спал. Он смотре́л на звёзды. Э́то бы́ло стра́нно.
exercises.en: I live in a city of glass. Every morning at seven we all get up, and every evening at ten we all sleep. The wall separating us from the forest is also glass. Today I saw, beyond the wall, a person who was not asleep. He was looking at the stars. It was strange.

exercises.text: Ста́нция на Ма́рсе рабо́тает уже́ сто лет. Лю́ди, живу́щие здесь, не зна́ют войны́. Ка́ждый рабо́тает сто́лько, ско́лько хо́чет, потому́ что маши́ны де́лают остально́е. Инжене́р говори́т мне: «Мы не лу́чше вас, мы то́лько ста́рше».
exercises.en: The station on Mars has been working for a hundred years already. The people living here do not know war. Everyone works as much as they want, because the machines do the rest. The engineer tells me: “We are not better than you, only older.”

glosses.войны: war (не знают войны: do not know war)
glosses.столько: as much (столько, сколько: as much as)

options: He was looking at the stars.
He was sleeping under the stars.

exercises.hint: I live in a city of glass.
We are not better than you, only older.

exercises.text: Э́то бы́ло стра́нно: он смотре́л на звёзды. Мы не лу́чше вас, мы то́лько ста́рше.

exercises.prompt: Your own science-fiction scene in four sentences.

units.title: The language of mathematics
units.subtitle: определе́ние · пусть, тогда́ · для всех, существу́ет · доказа́тельство

pages.title: Definitions
pages.intro: Every definition has the same shape: X называ́ется Y, е́сли…

exercises.text: A definition has one shape: X называ́ется Y, е́сли… . Мно́жество is a set, элеме́нт an element, принадлежи́т is belongs to; пусто́е мно́жество is the empty set. If and only if is тогда́ и то́лько тогда́, когда́ (the calque е́сли и то́лько е́сли is also heard).

examples.en: The number belongs to the set.

examples.ru: Число́ называ́ется чётным, е́сли оно́ де́лится на два.
examples.en: A number is called even if it is divisible by two.

examples.ru: Число́ называ́ется просты́м, е́сли оно́ де́лится то́лько на едини́цу и на само́ себя́.
examples.en: A number is called prime if it is divisible only by one and by itself.

exercises.hint: The number belongs to the set.
A number is called even if it is divisible by two.

exercises.text: Определе́ние. Число́ называ́ется просты́м, е́сли оно́ де́лится то́лько на едини́цу и на само́ себя́.

options: Two belongs to the set of even numbers.
Two is the set of even numbers.
Two does not belong to the set of even numbers.

exercises.text: определе́ние, едини́ца, тогда́ и то́лько тогда́, когда́

exercises.prompt: Define something simple in Russian: X называ́ется Y, е́сли…

pages.title: Theorem and proof: пусть, тогда́
pages.intro: A proof walks on a few words. Learn them and every proof opens.

exercises.text: A proof walks on a few words: пусть (let), предполо́жим (suppose), тогда́ (then), сле́довательно (therefore), отку́да сле́дует (from which it follows), противоре́чие (contradiction). A ле́мма is a small theorem on the way, a сле́дствие a corollary.

examples.en: Then the sum is also even.

exercises.text: Пусть… Предполо́жим… Тогда́… Отку́да сле́дует… Сле́довательно… Что и тре́бовалось доказа́ть.

options: From which it follows that the number is odd.
Suppose that the number is even.
From which it follows that the number is even.

exercises.prompt: A two-line proof with пусть and тогда́.

pages.title: For all, there exists, equals
pages.intro: Quantifiers, comparison and functions: the symbols, said aloud.

exercises.text: Для всех and для любо́го say for all; существу́ет says there exists; еди́нственный is unique. Равно́ is equals, бо́льше and ме́ньше are greater than and less than (with the genitive), and значе́ние фу́нкции в то́чке is the value of the function at a point.

examples.en: There exists a unique even prime number.
equals (the number after it goes into the dative)
the value of the function at the point two
the set of all even numbers

exercises.hint: Ten minus three equals seven (equals, not will be).

exercises.text: Три ме́ньше пяти́. Два плюс два равно́ четырём.
Существу́ет еди́нственное просто́е чётное число́: два.
Значе́ние фу́нкции в то́чке два равно́ четырём.
options: The function has two values: two and four.

Зна́чит, оно́ само́ просто́е и́ли де́лится на просто́е число́, кото́рого нет среди́ них. Получа́ем противоре́чие. Что и тре́бовалось доказа́ть.
exercises.en:
Theorem: there are infinitely many primes.
Proof: suppose there are finitely many of them. Consider the number: the product of all the primes plus one. Then it is not divisible by any one of them. So it is itself prime, or divisible by a prime that is not among them. We obtain a contradiction. Which was to be proved.

exercises.text: Philosophy's nouns are built with three suffixes: -ость turns an adjective into a quality (действи́тельный, действи́тельность), -ние and -ие turn a verb into an act or a state (мы́слить, мышле́ние; знать, зна́ние; быть, бытие́). pages.title: Socrates again, then Tolstoy
pages.intro: A dialogue in the old manner, and two sentences from the real books: Tolstoy's question, Dostoevsky's answer.

exercises.text:
— Что тако́е свобо́да? — спра́шивает Сокра́т.
— Э́то когда́ я де́лаю то, что хочу́, — отвеча́ет учени́к.
— А е́сли ты хо́чешь того́, что тебе́ вреди́т?
— Тогда́ я не свобо́ден, а раб свои́х жела́ний.
— Зна́чит, свобо́да — э́то не де́лать, что хо́чешь, а хоте́ть того́, что ну́жно?
— Ка́жется, так. Одна́ко кто реша́ет, что ну́жно?
exercises.en: “What is freedom?” asks Socrates. “It's when I do what I want,” answers the student. “And if you want what harms you?” “Then I am not free, but a slave of my desires.” “So freedom is not doing what you want, but wanting what is needed?” “It seems so. However, who decides what is needed?”

exercises.text: Лев Толсто́й в «И́споведи» спра́шивает: «Есть ли в мое́й жи́зни тако́й смысл, кото́рый не уничтожа́лся бы неизбе́жно предстоя́щей мне сме́ртью?» Достое́вский в «Идио́те», слова́ми кня́зя Мы́шкина, отвеча́ет: «Мир спасёт красота́».
exercises.en: Leo Tolstoy asks in A Confession: “Is there any meaning in my life that would not be destroyed by the death that inevitably awaits me?” Dostoevsky answers in The Idiot, in words attributed to Prince Myshkin: “Beauty will save the world.”
